_DURATION_RE = re.compile(
    r"\s*(?:(?P<days>[0-9]+)d)?"
    r"(?:(?P<hours>[0-9]+)h)?"
    r"(?:(?P<minutes>[0-9]+)m)?"
    r"(?:(?P<seconds>[0-9]+)s)?\s*"
)


def parse_duration(s):
    """Parse a duration string into a number of seconds.

    Units must appear at most once, in the order d, h, m, s.  A duration
    must contain at least one unit; bare numbers are invalid.
    """
    if not isinstance(s, str):
        raise ValueError("duration must be a string")

    match = _DURATION_RE.fullmatch(s)
    if match is None or not any(match.groupdict().values()):
        raise ValueError(f"invalid duration: {s!r}")

    values = match.groupdict()
    days = int(values["days"] or 0)
    hours = int(values["hours"] or 0)
    minutes = int(values["minutes"] or 0)
    seconds = int(values["seconds"] or 0)

    return days * 86400 + hours * 3600 + minutes * 60 + seconds
